own_solution.law: Newton's second law along the slope with kinetic friction: m a = qE cos(th) - m g sin(th) - mu_k (m g cos(th) + qE sin(th)); v = sqrt(2 a d) from rest
assumptions: horizontal field component into the slope adds to the normal force

T5CCF.regime: static friction coefficient below (qE cos th - m g sin th)/N = 14.243/12.048 = 1.182, so the block does start to slide

TA524.regime: static friction coefficient below about 1.18, so the block starts to slide

notes: qE = 18 N. Along slope: 18 cos25 = 16.3135 N; normal N = 0.5*9.8*cos25 + 18 sin25 = 4.4409 + 7.6071 = 12.0480 N; friction 2.4096 N; m g sin25 = 2.0708 N; net 11.8331 N; a = 23.666 m/s^2; v^2 = 37.866; v = 6.154 m/s. With m = 0.65 kg (charge unchanged): N = 13.3803, friction 2.6761, m g sin = 2.6921, net 10.9454, a = 16.839, v = 5.191 m/s. Toy-cart and earlier-trial sentences have no path to the target. T349D and T5A8D carry no number (numeral-free versions).
